target_customer: Operations and business teams at companies who want internal workflows automated without building them
problem: Internal operations rely on repetitive manual tasks and automation tools need setup and configuration. Cofia learns how a team works and builds automations itself.
product_category: AI workflow automation for internal operations

founders.name: Moses Wayne
founders.background_notes: YC page says Monetization he led passed 1 billion dollars annual revenue.

founders.name: Paola (Pao) Martinez
education: Stanford, CS undergraduate and MS&E master's
founders.background_notes: YC page lists 2019 Mayfield Fellows and Schmidt Futures Impact Fellow.

technical_complexity.rationale: Detecting repetitive work from activity and generating working agents or automations needs solid engineering plus reliability work, within reach of a small strong team using frontier models.

defensibility.rationale: Many workflow automation platforms add AI features. Learned knowledge of a team's operations could create switching costs if it compounds.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not yet observable. Directory comparison pages list Zapier, Gumloop, n8n and Relay.app as alternatives, but these pages are not dated to founding.

market_need_then: Companies were adopting AI agents for operations in 2025 and 2026 and automation setup effort was a known barrier. No Cofia-specific demand data found.

identity.visual_style: Not found; the site content was not retrievable
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, benefit-led tagline: AI automations that implement themselves

brand_strength.rationale: Short clean name but no press or community evidence on the brand. Search returned only directory listings.

outcome_analysis: Cofia is a Winter 2026 company, still active, founded by an ex-Duolingo engineering director and an ex-Brilliant product manager. No exit, shutdown or layoff reports exist. It is too early to judge. The main open question is whether self-implementing automations beat established workflow tools that are all adding AI.
notes: Funding unverified: directories (StartupHub, VCBacked and similar) list 500 thousand dollars in January 2026, labeled seed or pre-seed, with no investors and no primary source, so no round is recorded. The cofia.ai site fetch returned no content. Competitor sources are undated comparison pages so the list is empty. Outcome search found no acquisition, shutdown or layoffs. Completeness pass: the one recorded round rests on directory listings only (labeled seed or pre-seed, no investors named); no press or filing found.
